problem: AI coding agents cannot see what happens inside a real browser, so they struggle to debug pages or measure speed. This tool lets agents control and inspect a live Chrome browser.

stack.backend: TypeScript on Node.js, using Puppeteer to drive Chrome and the Model Context Protocol (MCP)
stack.ai: Works with MCP-compatible coding agents such as Claude, Cursor, Copilot and Gemini; includes Gemini-based evaluation scripts
stack.deploy: npm package run with npx (MCP server and CLI), plus plugin manifests for Claude, Cursor and Gemini

whatsNew: It gives an AI agent the real Chrome DevTools abilities (performance traces, network and console inspection, source-mapped stack traces) instead of just clicking pages. It is offered both as an MCP server and as a CLI.
